title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 263
paragraphs: Then for Dionysus, on the eve of the festival, each one kills a pig by cutting its throat before his own doors, and after that he gives the pig to the swineherd who sold it to him, to carry it away again. The rest of the feast of Dionysus is celebrated by the Egyptians in almost all respects just as it is by the Hellenes, except for choral dances; but instead of the phallos they have invented another contrivance, namely figures about a cubit high worked by strings, which women carry about the villages, with the private member made to move and not much less in size than the rest of the body; and a flute goes before, and they follow singing the praises of Dionysus. As to why the figure has this member larger than is natural, and moves it although it moves no other part of the body — about this there is a sacred story told.
